newsitem.title: USA: Stocks post strong gains; await start of earnings parade.
newsitem.headline: Stocks post strong gains; await start of earnings parade.

text.p: Stocks were sharply higher Tuesday, recovering strongly from the previous day's selloff amid optimism for the upcoming earnings reporting period.

At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow was up 67.85 points at 7,926.34, which was well above its July 3 record close of 7,895.81. The gain more than made up for Monday's 37-point drop, which stemmed from profit-taking.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 15-11 on active volume of 294 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index gained 9.46 points to 1,480.20 following further gains in technology stocks.
"The market is coming back from yesterday's late session sell-off, which is appropriate," said Paul Rich, a trader at BT Brokerage. "Technology stocks are strong, which is driving the market up."
The jump in technology stocks was led by Intel Corp., up 7/8 to 146-1/4, Microsoft Corp. up 1-3/8 to 130-7/8 and Compaq Computer Corp., up 4-3/4 to 119-1/4.
"The overall market is hopeful second-quarter earnings will be good, though the proof is in the pudding, of course," said Sam Stovall, analyst for S&P Industry reports.

Motorola Inc. was scheduled to report its second-quarter results after the market close. Analysts said they expected earnings to have grown slightly from last year's second quarter. Motorola rose 1-11/16 to 82-1/4.
Advanced Micro Devices Inc., which was also set to report after the close, rose 1-5/16 to 39-5/16.
Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd., said the stock market was also focused on the 8,000-point level for the Dow index.
"I think the market wants to peg 8,000 before we see any concerted profit-taking," he said.
Big-name blue chip stocks were also bolstered by a higher bond market.
The 30-year Treasury rose 2/32, lowering its yield to 6.57 percent from 6.58 percent Monday. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Gold stocks, which slumped Monday as gold prices fell, also made up some lost ground.

Barrick Gold Corp. rose 1-1/16 to 21-5/16 and Placer Dome Inc. added 3/16 to 14-3/16. The August gold futures contract was up $3.20 at $322.20 on New York's Commodity Exchange, rebounding from Monday's drop to $319.00 an ounce, the lowest price since 1985.
Salomon Brothers raised its rating on the gold stocks because of their recent erosion.

However, earnings warnings sent network software and systems tools stocks tumbling. Wall Data Inc. fell 9-3/4 to 18 after the software company said it expected its second-quarter earnings would be half of Wall Street's expectations.
Segue Software Inc. shed 4-5/8 to 8-1/2 after the company said its results would be disappointing.
